title: The Serre--Hochschild plane of a finite-dimensional algebra
summary: For a finite-dimensional algebra $A$ over a field we organize the Hochschild cohomology of $A$ with coefficients in all derived tensor powers of the Serre bimodule $ω=\D A$ into a single bigraded derived invariant, the \emph{Serre--Hochschild plane} $\T^{p,m}(A)$, defined over all of $\mathbb Z^2$ without inverting $ω$. The column $m=0$ is the Tamarkin--Tsygan calculus, $m=1$ is dual Hochschild homology (the column governing Han's conjecture), $m=2$ recovers the $τ$-Hochschild shadow, and $m=-1$ Keller's Calabi--Yau completions.
